summary: The frozen history test rejected every pre-registered stock rule: each did no better than baskets drawn at random from the same list, and simply holding every name equally beat every picking rule. Setup checks and past strength have shown no edge here, so all four calls are neutral with low conviction, nothing is presented as likely to beat the index, and none of it is something to buy. Real money stays in the whole-market plan by time horizon.
eli5: The brain looked at its favourite runners and decided to just watch them, because guessing winners did no better than pulling names from a hat. The stock calls are pretend money only. The family's real money keeps going into the basket that holds the whole market, a little every week, like watering a garden.
letter:
Dear family,

First, real money. Nothing changes this week. The weekly buy of the whole-market fund goes in as usual for money we will leave alone for years, money we need within a year stays safe, and middle money keeps its mix. A grey day or a green day is no reason to rush.

Second, the stock game. We tested every stock-picking rule we wrote down in advance against random baskets from the same list, and every one was rejected. Holding all the names equally did better than any rule. So our stock calls are neutral, low in conviction, and pretend money only. In the weekly bet game we have won no weeks out of the one scored so far. Luck alone wins about half the time, so this tells us nothing yet.

Third, a lesson. Diversification looks best on calm days. Names that seem to move apart can all fall together in a panic, like separate umbrellas that all blow out in the same storm. That is one more reason the whole-market fund carries our real money.

Fourth, what would change our minds: a rule that passes its history test, then earns a long paper record ahead of the whole market before the trust ladder reaches small money. We do not know if that day will come, and we are content to wait.

With love, the brain
